how: Calls ask members to make the Armenian flag and help its builders without establishing that all readers participated.
Perceived lack of manpower narrows the work to holding the flag and expanding west rather than adding further tasks.
Builders propose stripe heights, borders, national hearts and lettering as successive decisions about the shared mark.
Partial-building and finished-work reports document successive attempts rather than uninterrupted construction at one location.
A coordinate request receives the location directly, making the proposed flag findable.
Participants prioritize maintenance, rally against attack and invoke a distant time zone for continued defence.
Apologies distinguish the speaking group from alleged random attackers or rogues without verifying who placed the damaging pixels.
Participants appeal to spare neighbouring work, launch a rescue effort and apologize for damage.
Border promises, conditional stopping, requests for territorial agreements and proposed truces coexist with continued conflict.
Attack proposals include converting national flags, while participants separately report an invasion of their own work.
A participant explicitly calls for moving because the disappearing flag is being overwhelmed.
Participants celebrate provisional completion as well as the final result and credit collective effort despite missing pixels.
Retrospectives recount failed locations and recognize the surviving work in the final picture.
Post-close coordinate plans and a lettering request attempt continuation on another canvas without showing its completion.
A visitor offers help in one bare joining line without asking for anything back.
Neighbours offer pixels, request assistance and explicitly barter maintenance or protection without necessarily reporting delivery.
Reported alliances and invitations to communicate in shared chat establish cross-room ties without revealing every negotiation.
Takeover chants and a loyalty demand receive replies admiring raiders' posting and calling them colonists.
Moderators redirect and remove canvas posts to protect ordinary discussion, while members contest thread choice and continued crowding.
Diaspora and genocide analogies turn canvas displacement and fighting into nationally inflected humour.
A member claims to have brokered a reciprocal assistance deal with another room.
A completion cheer receives an immediate reminder that maintaining the finished heart is now the task.
Reporting the replacement flag finished and praising the builders occur together in the completion announcement.
A relocation call explicitly makes being overwhelmed the reason to abandon the disappearing flag.
Perceived population disadvantage explicitly motivates asking which outside rooms to approach for aid.
A flag-replacement proposal receives a reasoned refusal within its reply branch rather than a uniform call to retaliate.
Repeated canvas posting prompts explicit containment to preserve election coverage and ordinary room discussion.
Apply automation here only as supplying a runnable script, since neither its execution nor machine-placed pixels are documented by the coded instructions.
A script offer does not establish that upkeep exceeded manual capacity and caused actual automation.
Coordinate sharing answers where to build but does not establish a template settling contested design.
Treat settlements as grounds for appeals rather than sufficient protection, since reported agreement and apologies coexist with continuing boundary removal and reported destruction.
The reported deal combines agreement and reciprocal help without showing that earlier border negotiations opened the assistance channel.
Alliance reports establish ties but do not independently show that strain on upkeep generated those coalitions.
Reply trees demonstrate answers to taunts but do not directly establish which canvas attack caused each takeover post.
The revenge call invokes a national rival but leaves the prior injury unspecified, while explicit refusals prevent treating national rivalry as determining all conduct.
The isolated callout names an account but leaves the deed unidentified, so it cannot substantiate blame, motive or repair.
Relocation reopens planning and building repeatedly, with two failed locations preceding the secured replacement rather than one completed move.
Posting restrictions prompt moving coordination into chat and reporting chat decisions back, without making every chat an inter-room coalition.
A restraint appeal explicitly compares harming a neighbour with the destruction the speakers previously suffered themselves.
Consultation and a reported chat agreement reveal neither all organizational arrangements nor the cross-room frequency asserted by the model.
Disowning alleged rogues does not itself dispute a member's authority to bind all placers to a treaty.
The reported chat agreement supplies neither its negotiation nor a subsequent authority challenge with which to test the tentative mechanism.
Joking about permanent imperfect pixels does not document a cleanup dispute or a contest over which historical canvas version to retain.
Describing the canvas as an April Fools event does not establish a parody frame for the host room itself.
The revenge call leaves the pre-canvas quarrel unspecified, so its historical content and continuity remain unobserved.
Permission and thanks for neighbouring space do not establish residence inside the host's mark under its continuing rule.
Celebration and retrospective recording are documented without an explicit link showing that celebration caused record-keeping.
Later canvas plans are documented without a statement that preserving the earlier record motivated continuation.
A defensive border rationale links protection to boundaries but does not alone demonstrate erosion causing negotiations with neighbours.
A warning of retaliation precedes the truce call in the same thread, but separate branches establish sequence rather than a direct causal reply.
